Subject: Technical deep-dive recap & next steps (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Samir / Priya

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our technical deep-dive and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- Current latency: p95 ~= 700ms for contextual chat + retrieval-heavy requests.
- Peak throughput: ~150 requests/minute (bursty around business hours).
- Cost sensitivity: engineering leadership wants predictable unit economics before committing to a pilot.
- Data residency: certain PHI fields must stay in US-only VPC.

Goals we discussed:
- p95 latency target: <= 200ms for 95% of conversational generation requests (with typical context length ~512 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 200 req/s for search+generate mix during peak traffic.
- Pilot timeline: 4-6 weeks to validate latency and quality.

Model & infra requirements:
- Model family: we recommend testing an open LLM variant (Redwood-verified) with 8-bit quantization for cost/perf parity; full fp16 for quality-critical paths.
- Inference optimizations: prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational context, workload-aware batching, and dynamic kernel selection.
- Deployment topology: single-region dedicated pool (US-west) for pilot with cross-region fallback to US-east for DR; private VPC option for PHI.

Initial SLO proposal (attached spreadsheet):
- Latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 450ms (generation only).
- Throughput: baseline 50 req/s with autoscale to 200 req/s burst.

Action items / next steps:
1) Please confirm that the latency/throughput priorities above match your internal ranking (latency > throughput > cost).
2) Shared items needed from your side: representative request traces (anonymized), a sample 500-1k prompt set for eval, and a short summary of regulatory constraints for the dataset.
3) We'll circulate an SLO/architecture proposal and a deployment-template pack (see attachments) by EOD tomorrow.
4) If this looks good, we'll schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff w/ engineering (proposed Tue, Mar 16).

Attachments: acme_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO matrix, proposed test scenarios)

Thanks,

2) Data residency: we need the pilot to run entirely in our US VPC (no cross-border processing). Can Redwood support a private VPC deployment for the pilot?

Also, Priya wants a topology diagram and an expected minimum instance count for baseline/peak to present to infra. Can you include that in the architecture doc?

Hi Samir -

Quick answers and an initial topology recommendation that should address Priya's ask.

Private VPC: yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC for the pilot. We'll run inference in your VPC subnets and connect to our control plane via a secure connector; no model requests leave the VPC.

Quality & quantization: 8-bit quantization typically shows a small delta on conversational coherence for transformer-based open models. For your critical patient-facing flow we recommend:
- Pilot A: 8-bit quantized model to validate performance/cost (measure on your sample prompts).
- Pilot B (if quality regressions appear): fp16 run for critical endpoints; route lower-priority traffic to quantized variant.

Topology (pilot baseline):
- Region: US-West primary. DR: US-East fallback (cold).
- Nodes: start with 2 x NVIDIA A10/A100 instances in a dedicated pool (kept warm) with autoscale to 6 nodes for sustained high throughput. This gives us headroom for batching and KV cache efficiency.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts - expect ~20-35% token-cost reduction on chat flows.
- Batching: dynamic batching tuned to P95 latency target; continuous batching reduces cost but we'll tune to keep p95 <200ms.

Estimated pilot run-rate (very rough): $8k- $18k/month depending on instance type and utilization; we'll produce a tighter estimate once we see representative traces.

Attachments I'm sharing: redwood_deployment_templates.pdf (topology diagrams + config examples), acme_slo_matrix.xlsx (filled with baseline numbers and test scenarios). Links below for convenience.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_shared_architecture
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-ACME-2026

Let me know if you'd like an alternate node sizing (T4 / A10 / A100) - we can model cost/latency tradeoffs quickly.

Thanks,
